title: Time complexity and Big O
description: Learn how to measure and compare algorithm efficiency using Big O notation.

data.text: Not all code that works is good code. A program that solves the right problem can still fail if it takes too long or uses too much memory. Time complexity is the study of how an algorithm's running time grows as its input grows. Big O notation gives us a standardized language to describe that growth.

An algorithm that takes 1 millisecond on 10 items might take 10 seconds on 1,000 items. Another algorithm might take 2 milliseconds on 10 items but only 20 milliseconds on 1,000 items. The first algorithm has worse time complexity. As data grows, the difference between O(n) and O(n^2) becomes dramatic.

rows: Nested loops over the same list
Solving the traveling salesman with brute force

data.text: To find the Big O of a function, count how many times the dominant operation runs as a function of input size n. Ignore constants and lower-order terms. A loop that runs n times is O(n). Two nested loops that each run n times are O(n^2). A loop followed by a binary search is O(n log n).

data.title: Linear search vs binary search
data.content: Linear search checks every element. Binary search halves the search space each step.

data.title: Big O ignores constants
data.text: O(2n) simplifies to O(n), and O(n + 100) also simplifies to O(n). We care about how algorithms scale, not their exact timing on small inputs.

Many algorithms have different behavior depending on input. Binary search's worst case is O(log n), but its best case is O(1) if the target is exactly in the middle. Quicksort averages O(n log n) but worst-cases to O(n^2) on already sorted data with a bad pivot choice. Always know which case an interview question is asking about.

data.title: When to mention each case
items: Worst case — guarantees the upper bound under any input
Average case — expected behavior over typical inputs
Best case — the minimum work possible, usually less useful

items.question: Is O(n log n) better than O(n^2)?
items.answer: Yes, for large n. n log n grows much slower than n squared. Sorting algorithms like merge sort (O(n log n)) are preferred over bubble sort (O(n^2)) for large datasets.

items.question: Does Big O tell me the actual running time?
items.answer: No. Big O describes growth rate, not wall-clock time. A fast O(n^2) algorithm on small data can beat a slow O(n) algorithm on the same data.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Big O measures how work grows with input size
Common classes range from O(1) to O(2^n)
Always analyze worst case unless told otherwise
Choose algorithms with lower Big O for large datasets
data.takeaway: Big O notation is the shared language engineers use to compare algorithms objectively and choose the right one for the job.
